core_obligations: Strategy (proof lines 7017-7039): the author shows that the two adjunction maps are isomorphisms; the pullback of a sheaf is computed on objects as the value at the image object, and the pushforward is a limit over morphisms from such an image, so the composite of pullback and pushforward is a limit whose indexing category has an initial object given by the identity.

The counit (proof lines 7040-7084): uniqueness and existence of the components of such a limit are proved using conditions (4) and (3): condition (4) provides coverings on which the relevant morphisms into the image of an object factor through the functor, and condition (3) provides coverings on which two such factorizations agree, so the sheaf condition determines and produces the component.

The unit (proof lines 7086-7103): the value of the composite of pushforward and pullback at an object of the form u(U) is the value of the given sheaf, and condition (5) provides a covering of every object by such images, so the unit is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Show both adjunction maps are isomorphisms.
Compute the composite of pullback and pushforward as a limit and use conditions (3) and (4) to show the counit is an isomorphism.
Use condition (5) to propagate the identification from images of objects to all objects, giving the unit.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives sufficient conditions on a functor between sites for the associated morphism of topoi to be an equivalence: cocontinuity, continuity, two conditions allowing morphisms between images to be lifted and compared after a covering, and the condition that every object is covered by images of objects (statement lines 6990-7015). The proof is a complete argument: it reduces to showing that the two adjunction maps are isomorphisms (proof lines 7017-7039); the counit is handled by describing the composite as a limit over a category with an initial object and proving uniqueness and existence of the components using conditions (4) and (3) (proof lines 7040-7084); and the unit is handled by identifying the composite on objects of the form u(U) and using condition (5) to reduce every object to such images (proof lines 7086-7103). The non-formal content is the use of the covering conditions to control the limit. The claim is H2: a structured argument with every hypothesis used explicitly.
